title: Phoenix Union High School District Policies
description: Research and source links concerning Phoenix Union High School District policies.
body:
PXU proudly [shares](https://web.archive.org/web/20261028192753/https://www.pxu.org/o/pusd-210/page/district-information) that they are “one of the largest and most progressive high school districts in the United States.”

The District Information [webpage](https://web.archive.org/web/20261028192753/https://www.pxu.org/o/pusd-210/page/district-information) continues; “Diversity is a hallmark at Phoenix Union, with a population of 86% Latino, a large refugee population, and students who speak over 100 languages.”

Their PHX Student Bill of Rights [states](https://web.archive.org/web/20260911153207/https://www.pxu.org/page/student-bill-of-rights) that the district promotes “well-being in a safe space.”

The [district issued](https://web.archive.org/web/20260724225406/https://www.pxu.org/page/land-acknowledgement) a “Land Acknowledgement” dedicating their land to “22 sovereign nations of Arizona.

- They said “PXU understands the importance of providing reparations through truth-telling. We recognize the historical injustices not traditionally taught in the classroom and are committed to practices prioritizing Native American knowledge, history, representation, and healing. We commit with an open mind to always respect the land, its histories, and its ancestors.”

On their website, they [state](https://web.archive.org/web/20260724225406/https://www.pxu.org/page/land-acknowledgement); “The Phoenix High School District (PXU) is responsible and committed to creating educational environments that prioritize the achievements of Native American students. We are committed to making their cultural identity visible by acknowledging that our school district resides upon the ancestral lands of the original caretakers: The Hunugam, ancestors of the Akimel O’odham, Onk Akimel O’odham, Tohono O’odham & the Ak-Chin.”

They have an exclusive Native American Education Program.

- The school district [says](https://web.archive.org/web/20260918154409/https://www.pxu.org/o/pxu/page/native-american-program) the program “works to support and encourage academic, social, and extra-curricular success for all Native American high school students within [the] school district by providing culturally appropriate services, resources, and opportunities.”

- These programs grant an educational advantage to Native American students not afforded to students of other races. The program’s [staff](https://web.archive.org/web/20260918154409/https://www.pxu.org/o/pxu/page/native-american-program) “consists of one specialist and Native American student advisors…”

The school district published a video called “Vax to the Max,” establishing an 85% vaccination goal.

![Vax to the Max district video screenshot](/media/uploads/2026/11/arizona/pxu-vax-to-the-max-1.png)

![Vax to the Max vaccination goal screenshot](/media/uploads/2026/11/arizona/pxu-vax-to-the-max-2.png)

The district [named](https://web.archive.org/web/20260911152813/https://www.pxu.org/page/history) a high school after Cesar Chavez.

- The school opened in 1999 and underwent a name change to Cactus Canyon High School after the school board voted to rebrand the school. The vote came after sexual abuse allegations against the late Chavez arose March 18th, 2026, from National Farmworkers Association co-founder Delores Huerta.

The district also [renamed](https://web.archive.org/web/20260911154353/https://hoodline.com/2026/03/phoenix-high-boots-cesar-chavez-name-amid-sex-abuse-uproar/) their celebrations of Cesar Chavez Day.

- The name change correlated with the school’s name change. Phoenix City Council’s removal of Chavez’s namesake [preempted](https://web.archive.org/web/20260911155057/https://ktar.com/arizona-news/phoenix-council-removes-cesar-chavez) the school district’s actions.

School board members are [required](https://restoration-news.com/getContentAsset/9aff32d3-493e-4ef0-8f8f-a2b451cd8a18/347abc5f-3708-4979-a52d-d9fb8570b282/BIB-BOARD-MEMBER-DEVELOPMENT-OPPORTUNITIES.pdf?language=en) to be trained in “Anti-Racism/Educational Equity/Diversity/Inclusion.”

The school board passed the following resolutions:

- [Resolution to Advance Equity and End Systemic Racism](https://restoration-news.com/getContentAsset/6e816d3e-f4ef-4bb6-ae89-64d48c0e524a/347abc5f-3708-4979-a52d-d9fb8570b282/Resolution_to_Advance_Equity_and_End_Systemic_.pdf?language=en)

“Racial injustice and system racism persist in our country and community.”

“Law enforcement and criminal justice systems have a disproportionate negative impact on communities of color.”

The resolution refers to the deaths of George Floyd, Jamar Clark, and Michael Brown, as examples of “racially-biased police violence.”

“Police presence can be a source of fear and trauma, especially for students of color.”

“The District proudly supports the Black Lives Matter movement.”

“The District will not renew an intergovernmental agreement with the Phoenix Police Department for school resource officers.”

“The District renews its commitment to recruiting and retaining diverse employees and creating an inclusive workplace.”

- [Resolution Supporting Transgender Children and Youth](https://restoration-news.com/getContentAsset/3540c28b-a796-4125-b818-9a634b7680cb/347abc5f-3708-4979-a52d-d9fb8570b282/Resolution_Supporting_Transgender_Children_and.pdf?language=en)

Declares the district as standing in opposition to state legislation banning boys in girls’ sports.

“The Governing Board opposes legislation that is an attack on the safety of trans children and youth including legislation requiring them to participate in athletic competitions based on their sex assigned at birth.”

- [Resolution Opposing Expansion of Education Savings Accounts](https://restoration-news.com/getContentAsset/32b3918e-3f24-41a9-8d1d-f902242f91a6/347abc5f-3708-4979-a52d-d9fb8570b282/Resolution_Opposing_Expansion_of_Education_Sav.pdf?language=en)

“School governing board members… oppose the passage and signing of SB1431 into law and urge its reconsideration and repeal.”

- [Resolution Opposing the Adoption of HCR 2060 by the Arizona Legislature](https://restoration-news.com/getContentAsset/38f6d2f7-3add-4f86-8359-13f463043b8c/347abc5f-3708-4979-a52d-d9fb8570b282/Resolution_Opposing_the_Adoption_of_HCR_2060_B.pdf?language=en)

“The Arizona Legislature is considering House Concurrent Resolution (“HCR”) 2060 as an effort to selectively enforce immigration laws and penalize undocumented immigrants.”

“HCR 2060 will lead to racial profiling of immigrants and citizens because of the color of their skin, manner of speech, race, and ethnic origin.”

“The PXU Governing Board publicly denounces the adoption of the anti-immigration HCR 2060, expresses its abhorrence to the officials of the State of Arizona who support its enactment, and urges all members of the Arizona Legislature to vote against adopting HCR 2060.”

- [Proclaiming the Second Monday in October as Indigenous Peoples’ Day](https://restoration-news.com/getContentAsset/fad0ac35-6f36-4fa5-8818-8140c90a2bd4/347abc5f-3708-4979-a52d-d9fb8570b282/Proclaiming_The_Second_Monday_In_October_As_In.pdf?language=en)

“The Phoenix Union High School District Governing Board has a responsibility to oppose the systemic racism toward indigenous peoples in the United Stales, which perpetuates high rates of poverty and income inequality, exacerbating disproportionate health, education, and social crises.”

The “Governing Board seeks to combat prejudice and eliminate discrimination stemming from colonization and to promote awareness, understanding, and good relations among indigenous peoples and all other segments of our district.”

- [Love and Acceptance Resolution](https://restoration-news.com/getContentAsset/b4d1718a-4248-41ee-9108-76b81cda5115/347abc5f-3708-4979-a52d-d9fb8570b282/Love_and_Acceptance_Resolution_1-12-17.pdf?language=en)

“Phoenix Union values all lives equally - black lives, brown lives, disabled lives, undocumented lives, LGBT lives, gifted lives, refugee lives, female lives and any other category or subgroup or demographic that may be stigmatized; will love and accept everyone.”
The resolution states that is “standing behind the District's Deferred Action for Childhood Arrival’s (DACA) recipients and DREAMers regardless of changes in the law or policy.”

- [Resolution to Commit to the Resilience of PXU and the Community in Which It Serves (Official PXU Climate Action Resolution)](https://restoration-news.com/getContentAsset/96b959dc-374e-4151-9c06-30dfdfeb9df5/347abc5f-3708-4979-a52d-d9fb8570b282/Official-PXU-Climate-Action-Resolution.pdf?language=en)

“School districts are a major player in waste production, air pollution, and greenhouse gas emissions.”

“PXU is committed to performing a self-audit and report on the current standing of their environmental impact… Using this data, PXU will form an internal Task Force.”

“Efforts will be made to transportation within PXU more resilient through a commitment to transition PXU vehicles to more energy-efficient and less air-polluting vehicles, with a preference for zero-emission vehicles when possible.”

“PXU will incorporate grade-appropriate educational curricula in relevant classrooms and programs that equip students with sustainability knowledge applicable to tackling environmental challenges.”

- [Resolution Affirming Core Values, Equity, and the Dignity of All Students and Staff](https://restoration-news.com/getContentAsset/667cbc68-0404-4e5a-86ab-23931363b4d4/347abc5f-3708-4979-a52d-d9fb8570b282/PXU-Governing-Board-Resolution-Affirming-Core-Values-Equity-and-the-Dignity-of-All-Students-and-Staff20.pdf?language=en)

The resolution states the district “continues efforts to identify and remove systemic barriers” and commits to “inclusive decision-making that reflects the district’s diversity.”

- [Proclamation Declaring the First Friday in June to be National Gun Violence Awareness Day](https://restoration-news.com/getContentAsset/043532dd-62cb-41ed-af65-2cb407675b8f/347abc5f-3708-4979-a52d-d9fb8570b282/National-Gun-Violence-Awareness-Day-Proclamation.pdf?language=en)

“We renew our commitment to reduce gun violence and pledge to do all we can to keep firearms out of the hands of people who should not have access to them and encourage responsible gun ownership to help keep our families and communities safe.”

Former School Board Member Jeremiah Cotas was [stopped](https://web.archive.org/web/20260911160310/https://azfreenews.com/2026/02/phoenix-union-high-school-districts-lone-conservative-member-resigns/) from reading a prayer because he did not state the land acknowledgement.

- Petition for removal began following attendance at a Christmas party after a local Turning Point USA conference.
